svg.text: 🟣 Thought‑for‑the‑Day — Systemic Hollowing & the Measure of a Society

text.tspan: There is a strange dissonance in our age: a nation able to count 157 billionaires
can also count a record number of food banks. That contrast is not merely economic;
it is a moral measure of systemic hollowing. Across nine successive prime ministers,
the social contract has thinned, not through malice but through a long drift toward
a model of capitalism that rewards extraction over stewardship. CEOs answer to
shareholders, not citizens, and quarterly profit becomes the horizon of responsibility.
Yet a society cannot flourish when its economic successes and its human failures
grow in parallel. The true test of a civilisation is not the wealth it accumulates,
but the dignity it protects. If Magnifica Humanitas means anything today, it is the
reminder that human worth must not be collateral damage in an economic trajectory
that forgets the people it was meant to serve.
